chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about a slave owned jointly by partners, if one of them frees his share, he said: 'He is appraised for his value, and the one who freed him bears the guarantee/liability because he impaired the rights of his partners.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one partner frees a jointly-owned slave?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *daman* (guarantee) in partial manumission, where the freeing partner bears the cost of impairing the co-owners' rights. It reflects the Shia juristic consensus that voluntary acts affecting shared property require compensation to the other partners, ensuring equity in financial transactions.
